title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: Experimental package still development. encharter charting companion openxlsx2. treated first-class citizen : wb_add_encharter() lives directly openxlsx2, encharter integrates openxlsx2’s helper functions — wb_color() colors fmt_txt() rich-text formatting — wherever make sense chart context. package covers standard OOXML chart types (bar, line, scatter, pie, …) extended modern types Excel introduced later: waterfall, treemap, sunburst, box--whisker, funnel, region map.

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: ec() (short encharter()) creates R6 chart object. call methods add series configure chart, finally hand wb_add_encharter(). R6 objects mutate place, need reassign method call. Fig 1: first encharter chart
code: library(openxlsx2) library(encharter)  df <- data.frame(   Month = month.abb,   Sales = c(280, 295, 310, 340, 365, 390, 410, 400, 435, 460, 490, 520) )  chart <- ec("lineChart") chart$set_chart_title("Monthly Sales") chart$add_series(   name   = "Sales!$B$1",   label  = "Sales!$A$2:$A$13",   data   = "Sales!$B$2:$B$13" )  wb <- wb_workbook() |>   wb_add_worksheet("Sales") |>   wb_add_data(x = df) |>   wb_add_encharter(graph = chart, dims = "D2:K18")

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: Series data referenced cell range strings. two ways write . hand, using standard spreadsheet notation — sheet name, column, row, absolute: Via wb_data(), constructs range strings workbook object already data . avoids hardcoding cell addresses less error-prone data layout changes: approaches produce OOXML output. manual approach explicit easier read ranges simple fixed. wb_data() pays building charts programmatically source range determined runtime, feels native R. trade-offs . range approach possible assign custom series name cell reference — wb_data() approach name must correspond column data object. Multi-level legends, spreadsheet groups entries across two rows (example, age group label spanning male female series), achievable range approach. hand, features like drop-lines require construction wb_data() objects. examples use approaches interchangeably show equivalent; comment marks switch.
code: chart$add_series(   name   = "Sales!$B$1",   label  = "Sales!$A$2:$A$13",   data   = "Sales!$B$2:$B$13" ) dat <- wb_data(wb, sheet = "Sales", dims = "A1:B13")  chart$add_series(   name   = "Sales",   label  = "Month",   data   = dat )

text: chunks build single workbook. Run top bottom save end get encharter_examples.xlsx one sheet per chart type. sheet places data top-left corner chart directly right, basic table styling applied result looks reasonable opened.
code: # This section can be run standalone. The libraries are loaded again here # so these chunks work independently of the intro section above. library(openxlsx2) library(encharter)  wb <- wb_workbook(creator = "encharter")

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: line chart natural choice X axis time dimension story direction change rather individual values. show monthly headcount across two departments reader can compare trajectories glance. Fig 3: line chart
code: df_line <- data.frame(   Month       = month.abb,   Engineering = c(42, 43, 45, 46, 48, 51, 53, 53, 56, 58, 60, 63),   Marketing   = c(18, 18, 19, 21, 22, 22, 23, 25, 25, 26, 27, 28) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Line", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Line", x = df_line,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Line", cols = 1:3, widths = c(10, 14, 12)) wb_df <- wb_data(wb)  chart <- ec("lineChart") chart$set_chart_title("Headcount by Department", bold = TRUE) chart$set_x_title("Month") chart$set_y_title("Employees") chart$set_y_axis(min = 0, max = 80, major = 20, grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE")  chart$add_series(   name   = Engineering,   label  = Month,   data   = wb_df,   color  = "2E4057",   marker = "circle" ) chart$add_series(   name   = Marketing,   label  = Month,   data   = wb_df,   color  = "E84855",   marker = "circle" )  chart$set_legend_style(pos = "bottom")  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Line", graph = chart, dims = "E1:N18")

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: bar/column chart works well categories independent (time series) goal rank compare magnitudes. show quarterly revenue product line — fixed set categories size differences main point. Fig 4: bar chart
code: df_bar <- data.frame(   Product = c("Software", "Services", "Hardware", "Support"),   Q1      = c(310, 195, 140, 85),   Q2      = c(340, 210, 130, 90),   Q3      = c(375, 225, 125, 95),   Q4      = c(420, 250, 120, 105) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Bar", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Bar", x = df_bar,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Bar", cols = 1:5, widths = c(12, 8, 8, 8, 8)) wb_df <- wb_data(wb)  chart <- ec("barChart") chart$set_chart_title("Quarterly Revenue by Product (EUR k)", bold = TRUE) chart$set_y_axis(min = 0, format = "#,##0", grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE")  colors    <- c("2E4057", "048A81", "E84855", "F4A261") quarters  <- c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4") cols      <- c("B",  "C",  "D",  "E") variables <- names(wb_df) for (i in seq_along(quarters)) {   chart$add_series(     name   = variables[i + 1L],     label  = variables[1L],     data   = wb_df,     color  = colors[i]   ) }  chart$set_legend_style(pos = "bottom")  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Bar", graph = chart, dims = "G1:P18")

what: Stacked bar chart — part-to-whole over categories
title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: stacked bar shows total composed, composition shifts across categories. revenue data stacked show product line’s share total revenue per quarter. Fig 5: stacked bar chart
code: wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Stacked", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Stacked", x = df_bar,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Stacked", cols = 1:5, widths = c(12, 8, 8, 8, 8)) wb_df <- wb_data(wb)  chart <- ec("barChart") chart$set_chart_title("Revenue Composition by Quarter (EUR k)", bold = TRUE) chart$set_y_axis(format = "#,##0", grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE")  # using the range approach here (interchangeable with wb_data()) for (i in seq_along(quarters)) {   chart$add_series(     name     = sprintf("Stacked!$%s$1", cols[i]),     label    = "Stacked!$A$2:$A$5",     data     = sprintf("Stacked!$%s$2:$%s$5", cols[i], cols[i]),     color    = colors[i],     grouping = "stacked",     overlap  = 100   ) }  chart$set_legend_style(pos = "bottom")  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Stacked", graph = chart, dims = "G1:P18")

what: Combo chart — two measures, two scales
title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: two series different units different magnitudes, putting axis makes one unreadable. combo chart solves adding second Y axis. , absolute revenue (bars, left axis) shown alongside margin percentage (line, right axis). Fig 6: combo chart
code: df_combo <- data.frame(   Month   = month.abb,   Revenue = c(280, 295, 310, 340, 365, 390, 410, 400, 435, 460, 490, 520),   Margin  = c(.22, .21, .23, .24, .25, .26, .26, .24, .27, .27, .28, .29) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Combo", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Combo", x = df_combo,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Combo", cols = 1:3, widths = c(10, 10, 10)) wb_df <- wb_data(wb)  chart <- ec("barChart") chart$set_chart_title("Revenue & Margin", bold = TRUE)  # primary axis — bars for revenue chart$add_series(   name   = Revenue,   label  = Month,   data   = wb_df,   color  = "2E4057",   type   = "barChart" )  # secondary axis — line for margin chart$add_series(   name      = Margin,   label     = Month,   data      = wb_df,   type      = "lineChart",   secondary = TRUE,   color     = "E84855",   marker    = "circle",   line_width = 2 )  chart$set_y_axis(min = 0, format = "#,##0", grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE") chart$set_y2_axis(min = 0, max = 0.4, format = "0%") chart$set_y_title("Revenue (EUR k)", bold = TRUE) chart$set_y2_title("Margin", bold = TRUE) chart$set_legend_style(pos = "bottom")  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Combo", graph = chart, dims = "E1:N18")

what: Scatter chart — relationship between two measures
title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: scatter chart exploring relationship two numeric variables. axes continuous, unlike category-based charts . look whether pattern average deal size close rate across sales reps. Fig 7: scatter chart
code: set.seed(7) df_scatter <- data.frame(   Rep        = paste("Rep", LETTERS[1:12]),   AvgDeal    = c(14, 22, 18, 35, 28, 42, 19, 31, 25, 38, 16, 45),   CloseRate  = c(.28, .34, .31, .42, .38, .45, .29, .40, .36, .43, .27, .48) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Scatter", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Scatter", x = df_scatter,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Scatter", cols = 1:3, widths = c(10, 10, 12))  chart <- ec("scatterChart") chart$set_chart_title("Deal Size vs. Close Rate", bold = TRUE) chart$set_x_title("Avg Deal Size (EUR k)") chart$set_y_title("Close Rate") chart$set_y_axis(min = 0, max = 0.6, format = "0%", grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE") chart$set_x_axis(min = 0, grid_lines = TRUE, grid_color = "EEEEEE")  chart$add_series(   name        = "",   label       = "Scatter!$B$2:$B$13",   data        = "Scatter!$C$2:$C$13",   color       = "2E4057",   marker      = "circle",   marker_size = 8,   show_line   = FALSE,   trendline   = list(type = "linear", color = "E84855", show_r2 = TRUE) )  chart$set_legend_style(pos = "none")  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Scatter", graph = chart, dims = "E1:N18")  coef(lm(CloseRate ~ AvgDeal, data = df_scatter)) #> (Intercept)     AvgDeal  #> 0.183476102 0.006631492

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: waterfall chart breaks total contributing parts, making easy see drove increase decrease. common finance showing get one period’s profit next, gross revenue net income. Bars marked subtotals render running totals rather incremental steps. Fig 8: waterfall chart
code: df_wf <- data.frame(   Item  = c("Jan Profit", "New Clients", "Churn", "Upsell", "Cost Increase", "Feb Profit"),   Value = c(420, 95, -40, 60, -35, 500) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "Waterfall", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "Waterfall", x = df_wf,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "Waterfall", cols = 1:2, widths = c(16, 10))  chart <- ec("waterfall") chart$set_chart_title("Profit Bridge: Jan → Feb", bold = TRUE) chart$add_series(   name      = "",   label     = "Waterfall!$A$2:$A$7",   data      = "Waterfall!$B$2:$B$7",   subtotals = c(0, 5)   # 0-based indices; Jan Profit (0) and Feb Profit (5) are totals, not steps )  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "Waterfall", graph = chart, dims = "D1:M18")

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: box--whisker plot summarises distribution values — median, quartiles, outliers — one groups. useful want compare spread central tendency rather just averages. compare response times across three support tiers. Fig 9: box whisker chart
code: set.seed(42) df_box <- data.frame(   Tier  = rep(c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze"), times = c(40, 40, 40)),   Hours = c(     pmax(0.5, rnorm(40, mean = 2.5,  sd = 0.8)),     pmax(0.5, rnorm(40, mean = 6.0,  sd = 2.0)),     pmax(0.5, rnorm(40, mean = 14.0, sd = 4.5))   ) )  wb <- wb_add_worksheet(wb, "BoxWhisker", grid_lines = FALSE) wb <- wb_add_data_table(   wb, sheet = "BoxWhisker", x = df_box,   dims = "A1", table_style = "TableStyleMedium2" ) wb <- wb_set_col_widths(wb, sheet = "BoxWhisker", cols = 1:2, widths = c(10, 10))  chart <- ec("boxWhisker") chart$set_chart_title("Response Time by Support Tier (hours)", bold = TRUE) chart$set_y_title("Hours to First Response") chart$add_series(   label      = "BoxWhisker!$A$2:$A$121",   data       = "BoxWhisker!$B$2:$B$121",   statistics = "inclusive" )  wb <- wb_add_encharter(wb, sheet = "BoxWhisker", graph = chart, dims = "D1:M22")

title: Enhanced Office Open XML Charting for openxlsx2
text: encharter relatively young yet validate input OOXML standard. example, label position like "outEnd" works correctly bar charts may produce unexpected results line charts, check chart-type compatibility place. Test output using important files. Series cell references use standard spreadsheet notation: "Sheet1!$$2:$$10". sheet name required. extended chart types (waterfall, treemap, etc.), OOXML uses different XML schema internally (chartEx). encharter handles transparently — ec("waterfall") returns ChartEx object rather Chart object, interface . Radar charts accept filled = TRUE add_series() fill polygon interior. Bubble charts require third data range bubble sizes, passed weight add_series(). Bar direction (vertical column vs horizontal bar) set via dir = "col" (default) dir = "bar" add_series().

title: Encharter Base R6 Class — EncharterBase
text: Abstract base class inherited Chart ChartEx. Holds shared fields (palette, titles, axis params, legend/label settings) shared private helpers (render_color_core, render_color, set_axis_params, validate_input). Users instantiate EncharterBase directly; use encharter() instead.

title: Encharter Base R6 Class — EncharterBase
text: xml raw xml2 object containing chart space. series_data list containing added data series styles. type default chart type object (e.g., "lineChart"). palette character vector six-digit hex colors used series explicit color supplied. Defaults standard Office theme palette. chart_title Named list elements text (character) style (list font/fill/line options) main chart title. x_title Named list elements text style primary X-axis title. y_title Named list elements text style primary Y-axis title. chart_style Named list controlling outer chart area: fill (hex), line (hex), line_width (numeric). plot_style Named list controlling inner plot area: fill (hex), line (hex), line_width (numeric). label_params Named list global data label defaults: show_val, show_cat, show_legend_key (logicals), pos (character), style (list). legend_params Named list legend defaults: pos (character), overlay ("0"/"1"), style (list). axis_params Named list one entry per axis (x, x2, y, y2). entry named list scaling, formatting, style parameters. Modified via $set_x_axis(), etc.

text: Factory function initialises R6 chart object. Returns Chart object standard OOXML chart types (bar, line, scatter, ...) ChartEx object modern extended chart types (waterfall, treemap, ...). Chart class provides flexible interface build Office OpenXML (OOXML) chart objects. allows granular control grid lines, secondary axes, combined chart types (e.g., Bar Line) within single plot area. R6 class create manipulate Office OpenXML (OOXML) Extended Charts (ChartEx), including Waterfall, Sunburst, Treemap, Region Maps, supported standard Office Open XML chart types.

title: Create an Encharter Chart — encharter
text: Supported Chart Types: Bar/Column: "barChart", "barplot", "hist", "histogram" Line/Area: "lineChart", "line", "areaChart", "area" Scatter: "scatterChart", "scatter", "point" Pie/Doughnut: "pieChart", "pie", "doughnutChart", "doughnut" Extended (ChartEx): "waterfall", "treemap", "sunburst", "regionMap", "boxWhisker" / "boxplot", "funnel" Bar vs Column direction: bar/column charts, orientation set via dir argument $add_series(): "col" (vertical, default) "bar" (horizontal). class designed work openxlsx2 package generating underlying XML required add_chart_xml method. class uses XML manipulate underlying XML structure integrates openxlsx2 workbook generation.

text: name Cell range string series name. data Cell range series values. label Cell range category labels. weight Cell range bubble sizes (bubbleChart ). color Primary Hex color series (used default line markers). type Chart type specific series (combo charts). secondary Logical. Set TRUE move series secondary axis. dir Bar direction ("col" "bar"). grouping Chart grouping ("standard", "stacked", "percentStacked"). overlap Integer -100 100 bar charts. gap_width Integer 0 500 bar charts. smooth Logical. Enable line smoothing line/scatter charts. show_line Logical. Show line connecting points. marker Marker type ("none", "circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle"). marker_size Integer size marker. marker_fill Hex color interior marker. Defaults color. marker_line Hex color marker border. Defaults color. marker_line_width Numeric width marker border. show_val Logical. Override global label settings series (show value). show_cat Logical. Override global label settings series (show category). line_type Line style: "dashed", "dotted", "dashDot", "solid". line_width Numeric width connecting line. line_color Hex color connecting line. Defaults color. filled Logical; radar charts, fills interior area. Default FALSE. error_bars list error bar properties: type: error value type (ST_ErrValType). Must one : "fixedVal" (Fixed Value), "percentage" (Percentage), "stdDev" (Standard Deviation), "stdErr" (Standard Error), "cust" (Custom). value: numeric value error bars (e.g., 10 10% 5 fixed units). direction: Direction bars. One "", "plus", "minus". color: Hex color code bars (e.g., "FF0000"). trendline list regression line properties: type: regression type (ST_TrendlineType). Must one : "linear" (Linear), "exp" (Exponential), "log" (Logarithmic), "movingAvg" (Moving Average), "poly" (Polynomial), "power" (Power). order: Required "poly"; integer 2 6. period: Required "movingAvg"; integer representing window size. color: Hex color code line. show_r2: Logical; TRUE, displays R-squared value chart.
